Option surfaces from CME Globex settlements

Source: R/cme.R
cme_option_surfaces.Rd

Joins option and futures settlement prices to their instrument definitions and returns one row per valuation date, expiry, and strike, with the futures price as forward, time to expiry, Black (1976) implied volatilities, vega, log-forward moneyness, open interest, and a put-call parity diagnostic. The output feeds ec_theta_fit() (columns surface, k, iv, tau, and q when x is supplied), ec_mix_iv_pre(), and ec_quiet_library() directly.

Usage

cme_option_surfaces(
  definitions,
  statistics,
  assets = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  rate = 0,
  settle_time = "14:00",
  tz = "America/Chicago",
  invert = FALSE,
  min_price = 0,
  x = NULL
)

Arguments

definitions

Output of cme_definitions(), or anything it accepts.

statistics

Output of cme_statistics(), or anything it accepts.

assets

Optional product codes of the options to keep (for example c("6M", "1M", "2M")).

from, to

Optional first and last trading date.

rate

Continuously compounded annual interest rate for discounting: a number (default 0) or a function of (date, tau) returning one rate per row.

settle_time, tz

Valuation clock time and time zone (default "14:00", "America/Chicago").

invert

Logical; express prices per unit of the quote currency (see Details). Default FALSE.

min_price

Settlements at or below this value get no implied volatility (default 0).

x

Optional event_prices object; adds q, the last event probability at or before each valuation time.

Value

A tibble with one row per trading date, product, expiry, and strike: surface (identifier asset date expiry), date, valuation, asset, underlying, expiry, exercise, tau, F, F_final, strike, k (\(\log(K/F)\)), call, put, call_final, put_final, oi_call, oi_put, iv, iv_call, iv_put, otm (side used for iv), vega (price change per unit of annualized volatility), parity_gap, parity_gap_rel, F_parity, call_id, put_id, call_symbol, put_symbol (exchange symbols of the contracts used; with invert = TRUE the original put is the new call), and q if x is supplied.

Details

Which contract. Instrument identifiers are reused (see cme_definitions()), so each daily statistic is attributed to the definition phase in force on its trading date: the latest phase of its identifier that started on or before that date (UTC calendar of the daily definition snapshots), provided the next phase has not started, the phase was not deleted earlier, and the contract had not expired (trading date after the expiration date). Statistics outside every phase are dropped, including settlements dated before a contract's first definition record, such as the theoretical reference settlement the exchange sends with a new listing, dated the previous session.

Forward and timing. Each option is matched to its underlying future through underlying_id; the forward is that future's settlement on the same trading date. Where both symbols are published, the future's raw_symbol must equal the option's underlying; otherwise the forward is missing. The valuation time is settle_time on the trading date in time zone tz (14:00 Chicago time, the settlement time of CME currency futures and options); time to expiry tau is measured in years of 365 days from the valuation time to the published expiration. Options with tau <= 0 are dropped.

Implied volatility. Prices are discounted with \(e^{-r\tau}\) (rate) and inverted in the Black (1976) model. iv_call and iv_put are both reported; iv is the out-of-the-money side (calls at or above the forward, puts below it). Settlements at or below min_price, or outside the no-arbitrage interval, give NA. For American-style options (see exercise) the Black volatility is a European approximation; quantify the early-exercise premium separately (for example on a binomial tree) before relying on in-the-money quotes.

Inverted quotes. CME quotes currency futures in U.S. dollars per unit of foreign currency (for example 6M: dollars per peso). With invert = TRUE all quantities are re-expressed per dollar: forward \(1/F\), strike \(1/K\), calls and puts swap roles, and prices are converted with \(C'(1/K) = P(K)/(FK)\) and \(P'(1/K) = C(K)/(FK)\). Implied volatilities are unchanged and log-moneyness changes sign.

Parity diagnostic. parity_gap is \((C - P)/e^{-r\tau} - (F - K)\), in forward price units, and parity_gap_rel divides it by \(F\); F_parity is the forward implied by the call-put pair. Large gaps flag stale or mismatched settlements (American options can deviate slightly by construction).

References

Black, F. (1976). The pricing of commodity contracts. Journal of Financial Economics 3, 167–179.

See also

cme_definitions(), cme_statistics(), ec_theta_fit(), ec_quiet_library().

Examples

# one future and a call/put pair, priced at 10% volatility
F0 <- 0.0540; K <- 0.0545; tau <- 30 / 365
s <- 0.10 * sqrt(tau)
d1 <- (log(F0 / K) + s^2 / 2) / s
cl <- F0 * pnorm(d1) - K * pnorm(d1 - s)
pt <- cl - (F0 - K)
defs <- data.frame(
  instrument_id = 1:3, instrument_class = c("F", "C", "P"),
  asset = "6M", cfi = c("FFCXSX", "OCEFPS", "OPEFPS"),
  expiration = as.POSIXct("2016-07-01 19:00", tz = "UTC") +
    c(80, 30, 30) * 86400,
  strike_price = c(NA, K, K), underlying_id = c(0, 1, 1)
)
st <- data.frame(
  instrument_id = 1:3, stat_type = 3, stat_flags = 3L,
  ts_event = as.POSIXct("2016-07-01 22:00", tz = "UTC"),
  ts_ref = as.POSIXct("2016-07-01", tz = "UTC"),
  price = c(F0, cl, pt)
)
cme_option_surfaces(defs, st)[, c("date", "tau", "F", "k", "iv", "parity_gap")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   date          tau     F       k    iv parity_gap
#>   <date>      <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 2016-07-01 0.0822 0.054 0.00922 0.100          0
